newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Markka ERM debut smooth, stocks consolidate.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Markka ERM debut smooth, stocks consolidate.

text.p: The Finnish markka slipped smoothly into the European Union's currency grid on Monday, while major European stock markets consolidated recent gains.
The London stock market, Europe's biggest, edged to a new record close in modest turnover and Wall Street extended Friday's revival in quiet trading.

The Dow Jones industrial average of U.S. blue-chip shares, a key influence on European markets, broke back above 6,000 but trading was limited, with U.S. bond markets shut for the Columbus Day holiday and no major statistics set for release.
"The strength is a function of the lack of volume more or less," one U.S. share analyst said. "The absence of the bond market and the stable dollar are contributing to the strength."

Oil prices advanced, shrugging off last week's sharp fall amid renewed concern over winter heating oil supplies and tension in the Middle East. London November futures for North Sea Brent crude were up 60 cents at $24.58 a barrel in late afternoon trade.
EU finance ministers welcomed the markka's calm debut in the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), which limits the fluctuations of most EU currencies against each other.
But they were cautious about a quick return to the grid for the next candidate in line, the Italian lira.
After a finance ministers' meeting in Luxembourg, French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said the EU should not be too hasty in bringing the lira back into the ERM.
"To be hasty on the re-entry (of the lira) would mean to take a risk...which would cause harm to the Italian and European monetary authorities," he said.

In the latest step on the road to a single EU currency, Finland agreed at the weekend to put the markka into the ERM. One of the criteria for joining European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999 is at least two years of ERM membership.
The markka traded around 2.9880 to the German mark in late business, little changed from Friday's Helsinki close and stronger than its ERM central rate of 3.04.
But its widely signalled entry into the mechanism unsettled forestry stocks in Helsinki, although financial analysts said its rate should not put pressure on exporters.

Traders said the focus was now on the lira and the Swedish crown which, along with the British and Greek currencies, were the only EU currencies outside the ERM. Both the lira and crown ended firmer on the day.

With European currency news taking the spotlight and the U.S. holiday limiting activity, the dollar slipped a little although it was supported on any dips. The pound hit 2.4192 marks, its highest since January 1995, but eased back later.
European bourses, like Wall Street, had been in buoyant mood on Friday, rising on figures suggesting inflation in the United States, the world's biggest economy, was being kept in check.
London reversed early losses and gained more ground on Monday, aided by benign British producer price data and gains in U.S. stocks, to end just above the previous peak, set last week.
Dealers said sentiment was also boosted by a Merrill Lynch fund managers survey which said institutional investors were growing more optimistic about the British stock market.
But political jitters ahead of an election due by May are still a key background concern. "There's still the worry that this government cannot last the full term," one trader said.
French stocks ended easier in quiet trading, amid nervousness ahead of a public sector strike on Thursday, but the Frankfurt bourse made moderate gains.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5292 marks and 111.59 yen, compared with 1.5307 and 111.67 in late business on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 top British shares ended 10.6 points higher at a record close of 4,038.7.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt finished bourse floor trade up 7.85 at 2,693.88 and reached 2,700.83 in later computerised trading.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index ended down 3.50 at 2,143.62.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed London trading at $381.65 an ounce, up from its afternoon fixing of $380.90 and a previous London close of $381.35. Silver ended up three cents at $5.05.
